newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Sept 25.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Sept 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The University of Canberra's National Centre for Social and Economic Modelling used the Australian Bureau of Statistics' latest Household Expenditure Survey to compile an insight into the income and spending habits of the nation's most affluent. The survey showed not only are the rich getting richer, they are also spending a higher proportion of their weekly expenditure on luxury items. Page 1.

As Federal Cabinet deferred discussion on a review of cross-media rules, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission head Allan Fels said last night current foreign investment rules could restrict diversity of media ownership. The Howard Government is expected to abandon an election commitment to hold a public inquiry into media ownership in favour of an in-house review. Page 3.

Telstra officials last night were remaining quiet after the Community and Public Sector Union notified a dispute to the Industrial Relations Commission over management plans to revamp the national carrier's retail outlets, a move which would affect about 50 staff. Page 5.

The first Australian Financial Review/Telstra Australian Internet Awards named lone investor Gerry Pauley's Australian Stocks and Shares site on the World Wide Web as the Most Popular Australian Web Site, winning the award by public vote over the network. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Responding to Education Minister Amanda Vanstone's claims at a conference in Sydney on Monday that universities were not qualified to advise society on managing change because they could not manage it themselves, vice-chancellors yesterday attacked the Miister's suggestion that they were helpless as "hysterical", "misleading" and a "gratuitous insult". Page 1.

Controversial British right-wing historian David Irving, a revisionist historian of World War II who was denied a visa to visit Australia for a speaking tour due to his controversial denial of the Nazi holocaust, is challenging Prime Minister John Howard to prove his new climate of freedom of speech by overturning the ban on Irving's entry to the country. Page 1.

According to evidence presented to a Senate committee by Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade officials, a systematic fraud of A$70,000 from the Australian High Commission in Kenya was carried out under the noses of four diplomats without coming to light for three years. Page 1.

Following allegations that New South Wales Public Employment Office head Ken Cripps played a pornographic video to two 16-year-old boys after meeting them at a Sydney taxi stand in August, State Premier Bob Carr has moved to stand down Cripps, a long-time friend and political ally, from his position. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

According to the National Centre for Social and Economic Modelling's analysis of the 1993-94 Household Expenditure survey by the Australian Bureau of Statistics, the richest Australians donate the same share of income to charity as average households, but most of their spare cash goes on real estate and home improvements. Page 1.

China is likely to retaliate to tomorrow's meeting between Tibetan leader the Dalai Lama and Prime Minister John Howard by targeting Australian companies with commercial interests in Beijing. According to Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang, the meeting will certainly influence the political, economic and trade relationship between China and Australia. Page 1.

Following claims that Public Employment Office chief Ken Cripps showed pornographic videos to two 16-year-old youths, New South Wales Premier Bob Carr yesterday asked the top public servant to vacate his position. Cripps is also involved in an Independent Commission Against Corruption investigation. Page 1.

Under a proposal being drawn up by teams of high-ranking academics and administrators, the University of New South Wales would introduce larger classes, cut many small courses, abolish at least two faculties and reduce postgraduate student places by more han 900. The plan could also see 200 jobs disappear and the privatisation of many administrative services, such as maintenance and printing. Page 3.
THE AGE

According to a study by the University of Canberra's Ann Harding and Simon Fischer, Australia's richest 10 per cent are most likely to spend their money on their homes, their holidays, entertainment and their own convenience, but they give no more of their income to charity than other Australians - just 0.6 per cent. Page A1.

Diplomats and businessmen in Beijing believe Australian financial service companies with commercial interests in China are the most likely targets for retaliation from the Chinese Government, following comments yesterday by Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang, who said Prime Minister John Howard's meeting with the Dalai Lama would definitely cast a shadow over Sino-Australian relations. Page A1.

Federal Finance Minister John Fahey announced yesterday the aircraft maintenance workshops at Avalon Airport would be closed and 450 workers would lose their jobs after Federal funding was withdrawn because the board of Aerospace Technologies of Australia Aircraft Services told the Government that substantial losses were likely. Page A1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett yesterday contradicted statements by Prime Minister John Howard, claiming free speech in Australia has always been relatively unrestricted and although controversial Independent MP Pauline Hanson was entitled to express her views, Kennett said he totally disagreed with her stance on multiculturalism and she should be careful about making such comments just for short-term political gain. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
